chapter: Gulf Coast bands and early jobs
title: Tony Fougerat as best man and Margie
summary: Tony Fougerat played with him five years, was best man and pallbearer, and he still takes Tony's widow Margie to the doctor.

story.theme_name: Illness, injury and the deaths of colleagues
story.community_name: Illness, injury and death among jazz musicians

blocks.x: That's... You mean in the sense of playing like white musicians or in the sense of... Oh, sure. Yeah. Well, I think they're getting around to appreciating people. Fusier Wright was responsible for a lot of that somehow. They began to appreciate him. He was the one that they sort of fell in love with.

Tony and I were playing five years together before Ellen and I, my wife, met. And Tony was my best man at my wedding. Oh, yeah. We were married in Ellen's house and Tony lived one block from my wife. And Tony and I, I was one of Tony's pallbearers. And I still take Margie to the doctor. Oh, yeah? And she needs me to. I always take Margie and I always will until the day either one of us dies. Margie's 80, over 80. About 82 now. Almost totally blind. And she had to have me because I, you know, got a pretty strong arm and could take her, you know, and take care of her. She and Gloria and I, that's their oldest daughter, would take her to the doctor.
I can't remember Gloria. I remember Patsy.
